PullRequest.Title: sessions: Use first-prompt titles for Cloud Sandboxes
PullRequest.Body:

New Cloud Sandbox sessions currently lose their prompt-derived placeholder title during handoff and show the host default branch name, such as `main`.

This short-term workaround carries the draft title into the sandbox provider. Titles use the trimmed first prompt line, capped at 100 characters, with an explicit title taking precedence and `New Session` as the empty-line fallback. Both sandbox creation paths are covered; no model request is added.

Provisioning can return a client-seeded session before the host creates it. The sandbox provider retains renames for these provisional sessions and dispatches the latest title when authoritative host metadata arrives through a session-added notification or host listing. Discovery metadata does not trigger dispatch. Removal and eviction discard pending titles.

The merge with current main preserves sandbox setup progress and cancellation handling. Mission Control renames are persisted once before queuing the host update; a rejected task rename does not change or queue the title.

The host treats the resulting update as an explicit rename, so later runtime auto-naming will not overwrite the seeded title.

### Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/copilotChatSessions/test/browser/copilotChatSessionsProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --grep 'cloud sandbox send path|CloudSandboxSessionsProvider'` — passed, 107 tests.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/copilotChatSessions/browser/copilotChatSessionsProvider.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/copilotChatSessions/test/browser/copilotChatSessionsProvider.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/browser/cloudSandboxSessionsProvider.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Commit hygiene hook — passed.

Live validation on macOS, Code OSS 1.141.0 Dev, using isolated authenticated profiles and three real Cloud Sandbox sessions in `microsoft/vscode-mock-debug`:

| Variant | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original early-rename implementation, two fresh sessions | Both lost the short title. The client rename preceded host creation by 4.562 and 11.483 seconds. The host announced `main`; the UI showed it until the runtime later supplied the entire multiline prompt as a fallback title. |
| Retained-title follow-up, one fresh session | The host accepted the short title after announcing the session. The first turn completed, reopening retained the title, and a fresh host `listSessions` independently returned the exact short title. |

No artificial startup delay was introduced. The live-tested flow was desktop Cloud with Sandbox selected; the dedicated web creation picker was not exercised live. All three validation sessions were deleted afterward.

Manual verification: start a Cloud Sandbox session with a multiline prompt and confirm that the title remains its first line after provisioning, the first response, and reopening.

(Written by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed await, handler binding, HTTP implementation, 10-second timeout, and following send call are all directly traced. The only magnitude uncertainty is typical Mission Control latency; the critical-path network round trip is unconditional for this creation flow.
Findings.PerformanceResource: one Mission Control HTTP PATCH per newly created sandbox session
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is one additional serialized network request for every Cloud Sandbox creation; concurrent creations each issue their own PATCH, while each individual first turn cannot progress until its PATCH completes.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased latency and a blocked first-turn critical path
Findings.PreviousBehavior: After sandbox preparation and model carry-over, the code dispatched the first chat request immediately; no task-title HTTP request was on this segment of the first-turn critical path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every new sandbox first turn now serially waits for a Mission Control task-title PATCH to complete before the chat request is dispatched.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1758 adds `await raceCancellationError(provisioned.provider.renameSession(...), token)` immediately before `provider.sendRequest`; the provisioned CloudSandboxSessionsProvider has a task rename handler bound by CloudSandboxAgentHostContribution to `_renameSandboxSession`, which awaits `ICloudSandboxApiService.renameTask`, an HTTP PATCH with a 10,000 ms timeout.
Findings.Title: Do not block the first prompt on task-title persistence
Findings.Impact: Starting a Cloud Sandbox session incurs an extra control-plane network round trip before the user's prompt reaches the agent, increasing time to first response by the PATCH latency and potentially by up to the request timeout on a slow service.
Findings.Evidence: `provisionSession` calls `_ensureProvider` with the newly created task/session IDs, which binds `setTaskRenameHandler(... _renameSandboxSession ...)`. `CloudSandboxSessionsProvider.renameSession` awaits that handler before queuing/updating the title. `_renameSandboxSession` awaits `_apiService.renameTask`, and `CloudSandboxApiService.renameTask` performs a PATCH using `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000`. Only after the added await resolves does line 1759 call `sendRequest`.
Findings.Recommendation: Queue/apply the initial host title before sending, but move Mission Control title persistence off the prompt-dispatch critical path (for example, use a dedicated initial-title operation that installs the pending host title immediately and persists the task title asynchronously with explicit error reporting).

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a Cloud Sandbox and send its first prompt
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provisioning, connection, repository preparation, model carry-over, the new title PATCH, and then chat dispatch are serialized. The added PATCH must now complete before the user's first prompt can be sent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the Mission Control sandbox task/session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One task-creation HTTP request per new sandbox.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same task-creation request was already required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete to obtain the environment and session before creation can continue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connect to the remote sandbox and prepare its repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One connection/wake attempt and one preparation operation per new sandbox.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These boundaries were already on the creation critical path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both complete before the first prompt can be sent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the prompt-derived title to the Mission Control task.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one PATCH per sandbox creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No title-persistence request occurred between model carry-over and prompt dispatch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The added await blocks prompt dispatch until the PATCH returns, with a 10-second request timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the user's first prompt through the connected agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Starts agent work and time to first response, but now starts only after title persistence.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional request per newly created Cloud Sandbox session; concurrent creations produce one request each.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within one creation these operations are serial. Separate sandbox creations are not globally limited here and each adds its own PATCH.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new title PATCH is unconditional and has no response cache; authentication state may already be warm, but every created sandbox still performs the PATCH. The provisional-title map keeps only the latest title per raw session ID.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added await is directly connected through the bound rename handler to an HTTP PATCH, immediately preceding sendRequest.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical Mission Control PATCH latency is not measured, but the unconditional serialized round trip and 10-second timeout budget establish a real latency mechanism; severity is medium rather than high.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: an unconditional control-plane network call was added to the first-turn critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reconcile a provisional session after delayed host creation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A provisional rename waits for Mission Control persistence before it enters the pending-title map. Later host listing or session-added metadata flushes one title action; that flush does not wait for a host acknowledgement.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive authoritative session metadata from the agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing host listing when refresh discovers the materialized session, or one session-added notification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The host metadata path already listed or notified sessions but did not flush a pending initial title.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Establishes authoritative host metadata; listing latency is pre-existing, while notifications arrive asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch SessionTitleChanged after the host materializes the session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one title action for the latest pending title per provisional session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No deferred title action was emitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dispatch is invoked synchronously during metadata reconciliation but does not await a remote response, so it adds only one enqueue operation to that path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously provisional sandbox sessions, effectively one entry per session and one latest title per key.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Latest-title replacement coalesces multiple provisional renames to one pending value. Each cloud provider normally owns one sandbox session, so authoritative discovery flushes at most one queued title for that provider.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Pending titles are keyed by raw session ID, overwrite older titles for the same session, and are removed on authoritative metadata, host/local removal, or provisional eviction. There is no unbounded duplicate accumulation per session.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: map replacement and all normal cleanup/flush paths are explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host materialization timing varies, but effective cardinality is bounded to one pending title and one dispatch per session.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional report: the pending map is lifecycle-bounded and coalesces by session; the single deferred IPC dispatch is required for the feature and is not awaited on a remote acknowledgement.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rename an already materialized Cloud Sandbox session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Mission Control task rename is awaited and then the host title action is dispatched, matching the pre-diff order for non-provisional sessions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist and propagate a user-requested title change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One Mission Control PATCH and, when connected, one host title dispatch per user rename.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior handler-matched branch already awaited the same task rename and then called the same base host rename.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The rename command waits for task persistence as it did before this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One operation per explicit user rename.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One user rename operation performs one task PATCH and one host dispatch; no new fan-out or concurrency was introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing sessions are not provisional, so no pending-title entry is created. No new cache behavior applies.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from direct before/after branch comparison.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to PR causality; the boundary count is unchanged for non-provisional sessions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the refactor preserves the pre-existing boundary count and ordering for this scenario.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remove or evict a provisional sandbox before host creation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Removal and eviction perform constant-time map deletion with no new external boundary.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live provisional sessions, with one short title string per session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cleanup is synchronous and per removed session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Queued titles are explicitly deleted on local deletion, host removal, and provisional eviction; provider disposal releases all maps with the provider.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: every existing provisional retirement path touched by the change also removes the pending title.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None; cleanup sites are explicit, though provider lifetime determines how long a still-valid provisional entry remains.
Scenarios.Verdict: No retention regression: pending title lifetime follows the already-bounded provisional-session lifecycle.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files. One medium-confidence-in-magnitude, high-confidence-in-mechanism issue was submitted: first-turn dispatch now serially waits on a new Mission Control title PATCH. Pending-title retention, reconciliation, cleanup, and existing-session rename behavior are bounded or unchanged.
